paper_title: SepLLM Accelerate Large Language Models by Compressing One Segment into   One Separator
caption: The loss comparison between vanilla Transformer and the proposed SepLLM. SepLLM achieves lower loss different computation costs and different training time consistently.
model_annotation: The plot illustrates training loss over time for two model variants, showing how loss changes as training time increases. The x-axis is labeled “Training Time (s)” and uses a linear scale ranging from 0 to 250,000 seconds, with regularly spaced tick labels at 50,000-second intervals (0, 50,000, 100,000, 150,000, 200,000, 250,000). The y-axis is labeled “Loss” on a linear scale from 2.40 to 2.75, with tick labels at 0.05 intervals (2.40, 2.45, 2.50, …, 2.75). Two solid lines are shown: a purple line with triangle markers labeled “Vanilla,” and a red line with circular markers labeled “SepLLM.” Both lines decrease over the full x-range: the Vanilla curve starts near the top of the plotted range (just below/around 2.75 at the earliest visible times), declines to about 2.62 around 50,000 s, about 2.57 around 100,000 s, about 2.54 around 150,000 s, and ends near 2.50 at 250,000 s; the SepLLM curve begins around 2.71 at the earliest visible times, drops to about 2.61 around 50,000 s, about 2.56 around 100,000 s, about 2.53 around 150,000 s, reaches roughly 2.50 around 200,000 s, and continues to about 2.49 by roughly 230,000–240,000 s. Green dashed reference lines and an annotation mark a horizontal level at loss = 2.50, with vertical dashed lines at approximately 200,000 s and 250,000 s, and a green bracket between these verticals labeled “1.26×.”
